newsitem.title: FRANCE: France urges its nationals to leave Zaire.
newsitem.headline: France urges its nationals to leave Zaire.

text.p: France urged its nationals to leave Zaire on Thursday in the light of political uncertainty there and sent extra troops and aircraft to neighbouring countries in case it needs to protect them.

"Given the uncertainty linked to the current situation in Zaire, the French authorities recommend that citizens whose presence is not essential leave the country temporarily. This precaution applies particularly to families," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said.

The Defence Ministry earlier said three transport planes, two helicopters and 100 soldiers had been flown to neighbouring Congo and Gabon as a precaution to protect and evacuate French nationals from Zaire if necessary.

Rummelhardt said there were about 1,500 French citizens in the sprawling central African country, where rebels have captured a swathe of eastern territory. More than 900 of the French expatriates live in the capital, Kinshasa.

Ailing Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko is planning to leave France on Friday, after undergoing further cancer treatment in Monaco, and return to Kinshasa to seek a political solution to the fast-spreading rebellion, his son said.
